reviews.author: Mack
reviews.text: Bullards Beach State Park is one of my favorite places to go. I don't live far away from it and it was the first place I camped at when I moved back to Oregon. I highly recommend it for vacation. Great yurts. It also has a wonderful horse campground.

reviews.author: Lionel W
reviews.text:
Great park.
The RV parking pad is absolutely level and private.
Men’s shower room is spotless.
The trail is well maintained and the view is great.
Quiet and dark at night.
Great price ($42 for non OR resident with power and water).

reviews.author: LB
reviews.text: Well taken care of campground. Quiet, clean and beautiful. Bullards Beach State Park is a gem and central to many day trips...Port Orford,  Cape Blanco, Seven Devils State Park, Charleston and the three State parks there including Cape Arago, Coos Bay...on and on. We will visit again. I n87sgXCeKcQ

reviews.author: Catherine Olivolo
reviews.text: It's a wonderful state park. There are lots of spaces, rvs yurts, tents. Hiking trails; close to the ocean. 2 miles north of Bandon.

reviews.author: Carey Grayson
reviews.text: State campground. Nicely maintained. Water and electric only, no sewer but there is a dump station. Close to the beach and hiking trails. Located just outside of town.

reviews.author: Easygojoe
reviews.text: This campground is orderly and clean. People seem respectful and there are numerous hosts. It’s quite large. Very coastal feeling. You can drive to the beach or you can hike it, which is about 3/4 of a mile.

reviews.author: camper-850729
reviews.text: We loved our stay here, the sites are spread out with lots of plants and trees between them. Facilities were clean.

reviews.author: DrBob806
reviews.text:
We had fun here, great beach & scenery. Campsites are fairly close together, not a lot of privacy but it's still a good place.

Make sure you visit Face Rock SP down the road (6 miles) & Old Town Bandon.

Camp workers really keep this place clean. FHU at most of the sites ( B loop closed at this time).

When we visited in March, only the C Loop was being used. We had full hookups. We had privacy on 2 sides with shrubbery. The Stellar Jays and Turkeys roam the campsites.

The decommissioned Coquille River Lighthouse is 3 miles away, and the beach is 1.5 miles away. There is a shorter trail leading from the back of B Loop, but it was underwater, about .25 miles from the loop.

The campground is just north of Brandon, OR.

reviews.author: camp-roadtripper351930
reviews.text:
This was the third campground stop along the Oregon coast in October 2023. Had to wait a bit to get in because this is a very popular place. The campground is in good condition, with easy access to bathrooms and showers if you are in need of them. I missed that my site had no power, but there was power at many of the sites, not quite sure what the power layout was, my bad. Plenty of trail on the campground property in my case to walk the dog. Overall, I would say a congenial group of campers, no rowdiness; makes it a good place to sleep.

Short drive to downtown Bandon and the beaches.

reviews.author: J.-Taylor
reviews.text:
Camped with horses in the Equestrian Camp. Loved this place! Only .3 miles from the beach! We could hear the waves crashing constantly! Great corrals at each site. Dry camping. Water available. Phone service was good, but no internet.

I do hate it when they make you move the next day from an open first come, first serve site, showing as Available on the reservation website, and then no one ever comes! Made us move from the shade to the sun. What’s up with that?

Great rangers.

Great place! Loved it!!

reviews.author: camper-723623
reviews.text: As other reviewers pointed out, the beach is actually a mile away, but that just made for a nice walk to get there, through a lovely wooded and wetland landscape. The beach was windswept and deserted and oh so beautiful. We stayed in A10 which was less private than other sites further around A loop. Sites were spaced out enough for it not to be an issue for us, but there was some traffic noise as the site was fairly close to the entrance road. Wild turkeys roaming around the campground were fun to watch. Showers were hot and clean, bathrooms clean too with no-touch soap and faucets which is great. Trash compactor available at the exit of A loop, and recycling facilities a short walk away too. We did have to line up for the single dump station when we were leaving, but it wasn’t too long a wait. Overall, another great experience at an Oregon State facility.

reviews.author: Tin Tumbleweed
reviews.text:
Verizon speeds were very inconsistent, sometimes dropping to 3Mbps. Most of the time it was 30Mbps download and 8 Mbps upload. T-Mobile was 50/1. Both with a roof mounted Pepwave antenna.

This is a good state park, but we enjoyed Harris Beach down the road more for the views and beach proximity. Our site was level, but had a wide and shallow pothole that held rainwater during our stay. Sites are reasonably large with dense shrubs between for privacy. There is only one dumpster for the entire A loop and it's at the entrance. The beach is actually about a mile away.

Later in the week we had a brief low voltage issue with heavy draw that triggered our EMS.

reviews.author: Babs5024
reviews.text: Nice clean campground. Sites are a little tight for 30 foot trailer and tow vehicle.

reviews.author: thedrivingdeveros
reviews.text:
Stayed in B60. Spaces appeared relatively flat, very clean campground, decent privacy from side-to-side but can see anyone very well across from you.

Biggest complaint was the showers didn’t close their doors, and you can’t control water temps. So, it was warm water (not hot) with a drafty bathroom. The beach and lighthouse are a bit of a walk to get to.

2 bars workable Verizon and ATT.

reviews.author: Trillium41
reviews.text: We had a lovely 2 day stay at this campground near Bandon, Oregon. The campsite was spacious and paved. Trees and bushes separate campsites so you have a nice feeling of privacy. The clean scent of evergreens fill the air. We enjoyed walking along the driftwood strewn beach and seeing the lighthouse. The lighthouse has a gift shop open in the afternoon; however we didn’t arrive until after 5. Watch out for the mosquitos - they are in waiting to welcome us visitors. Bandon has several nice, city beaches with clean restrooms! We loved the Face Rock area. We also enjoyed Tony’s Crab Shack on the old town boardwalk, delicious fish tacos. There are many sculptures, wood carvings, and statues to enjoy. It was fun to watch families crabbing along the waterfront. An added bonus was the seals bobbing around trying to steal the bait. We would love to come and visit again!

reviews.author: Hopefull1995
reviews.text: Nice campground with beach access and Coquille lighthouse. Lots of places to picnic and enjoy the day. We camped here and the amenities are great.

reviews.author: Teresa W
reviews.text:
We were very impressed with the variety and number of campsites. Each one was lighted and maintained immediately after each camper left. The showers weren't real hot, but had good pressure and privacy. While we would definitely stay here again, we would not buy the $5 bundle of firewood as it did not seemed to be seasoned properly. The wood smoked too much and kept going out, needing to be re-lit several times. The hosts and registration personnel were all very helpful and friendly. I'm not sure if they offer wifi, but we did pick up a signal and were able to use our tablets during our 3 day stay.
Room tip: Loops A & B seemed to have more privacy between campsites than Loop C

reviews.author: K S
reviews.text: Bullards doesn't feel as large as it is because of the 3 loops. Bathrooms and showers were very clean. Lots of attendants. With all the ponds nearby, we weren't surprised to see mosquitos in morning and evening. A sunnier camp spot may have helped. We were on the west side of loop C. The north and east sides were sunnier. We loved the trails to beach. About 1/2 mile walk. We plan to return!

Spend 4 nights here in August. Site was clean, bathroom was clean, and the C loop includes an accessible restroom with additional signage asking the non-disabled to use a different restroom, which most campers honored. This campground does not do cash transactions, I had to use a credit card to buy wood and fire starters, and the hosts only sell these items between 4pm - 8pm. No critters tried to get into my cooler or garbage at night. The park has a large day use area with plenty of room to find your own space. Lots of sights and activities in the area. Photographers can obtain night photography permits for the Face Rock Viewpoint for free. I got a nice shot of the Perseids over Face Rock at around 11 pm.
